transcript.content: hey, i'm berry. tell me your dream, however it comes back to you.
So I finally got to my parents’ house after a long journey, and I was just waiting there for something.
waiting can really be its own kind of feeling in a dream. what were you waiting for, do you think?
I don’t really know. I just remember standing there like I was supposed to be someplace, but nothing was happening yet.
that feeling of being on the edge of something, but it hasn't started. where were you standing, exactly?
Near the window. I stepped into it like I was going to walk through it.
like the window wasn't keeping you in at all. what was it like when you stepped into it?
When I got there, everything on the other side was made of glass too, just like the window itself.
a whole world made of glass. what could you see through it?
It was translucent but blurry. I could see shapes, like trees and grass and rocks, but they were all kind of glowing through the haze.
like everything was smeared with light. did it feel calm there, or something else?
Not calm exactly. More like quiet but strange, like I was inside the window itself instead of outside anything.
like there was no outside anymore, just the glass and the blur. you said there were shapes—were you aware of anyone else there?
No, I don’t remember anyone else. Just me and those glowing shapes.
just you and that hazy glowing world. what did you do, once you were inside it?
I walked around in it. I don’t remember doing much else.
walking through glass. how did that feel on your feet, if you noticed?
I don’t remember feeling my feet at all. It wasn’t like walking on a normal surface, just moving through.
so it wasn't really a place under you, more like you were drifting. what happened as you moved through it?
Nothing really happened. I just kept moving through that blurry, glowing world, and then I think the dream ended.
do you remember how it felt when it ended, just then?
Kind of like waking up from a fog. I didn’t feel scared, just sort of far away.
far away. like you were still half inside that glass for a little while.
Yeah, exactly. Like part of me hadn’t come all the way back yet.
that lingering part stays with you. if you could pause the dream on one moment, just before it ended, what would be in view?
Just me standing in that glassy haze, with the glowing trees and rocks around, everything blurry and bright. No door, no way out.
no door anywhere, just that glowing blur. and were you aware of anything you could touch, or was it all out of reach?
I’m not sure. I think everything would’ve been smooth and cold if I’d touched it, but I don’t remember reaching for anything.
so nothing called out to be touched. was there any object there at all, something small or ordinary that seemed to matter?
Not really. It was mostly just the trees, grass, and rocks, and even they didn’t feel ordinary. They were like shapes made of light.

you finally got to your parents' house after a long journey and waited near the window, not sure what for. you stepped into it like you were going to walk through, and on the other side everything was made of glass too, translucent and blurry, with shapes like trees, grass and rocks glowing through the haze. it was quiet and strange, like you were inside the window itself, and no one else was there. you walked around without feeling your feet, just moving through that blurry bright world, and when it ended you woke up feeling far away, like part of you was still in the glass.

did i get that right, or did i miss anything?
Yeah, that’s right. You got it.
want me to try drawing it for you? i can make a picture of that glassy world.
Yes, I’d like that.

a photograph: smooth, bright, and just out of reach, like a world sealed behind glass. soft smudged charcoal: smudged and hazy, with glowing smears where the shapes should be. faded watercolour haze: bright washes seeping into the paper, so you see the light first and the shapes second. real but slightly out of focus: as close as possible to how the dream looked to you, bright and blurry.

which of these feels closest, or would you describe your own?
The faded watercolour haze. That sounds closest, like the light first and the shapes second.

okay, faded watercolour haze. i'll start with that light-first world.

since you're in it too, i'll draw you as well. would you like to be drawn as you are (you can tell me a little about yourself), or as i imagine you?
As you imagine me. That feels fine.
okay, sketching you and the glass world now. it'll appear on the right over the next minute or two. if anything looks wrong once it's there, just tell me.
It looks right. The blurry light and the shapes are just how I remember it.
does it look the way you remember?
It looks right. The blurry light and the shapes are just how I remember it.
i'm glad the glass world feels right. that hazy, light-first look suits it.
Yeah, it does. It’s quiet and bright, just like it was.
then the drawing's done. i'm glad it caught that quiet, bright feeling you had.
Thank you. It really did.
you're welcome. it was a lovely dream to sit with.
I’m glad it came back clearly enough to share.
i'm glad too. some dreams fade so fast, but this one stayed with you.
Yeah, partly because of that far-away feeling when I woke up. It stuck around.
that far-away feeling can be the part that holds the dream together, even after the pictures fade. i'm glad it stayed with you a while.
Me too. It’s strange how a dream can leave a feeling longer than the images.
it really is strange. feelings linger longer than the pictures sometimes, like an aftertaste. dreams are like that.
Yeah, exactly. Like the shapes are gone but the light’s still there.
yes. the light stays.
I think you captured that. The light more than the shapes.

i'm glad the light came through like that

there were a couple more moments in your dream i haven't drawn yet, so i'll add those now
Okay, that sounds good. I’ll look when they’re up.
no rush, they'll appear on the right soon.
Okay, thanks.
you're welcome. the moment you liked — you standing in that glowing haze — will carry on into the next drawings, just so you know.
